metadata.proof: Same pattern as export_matters_csv: Deadline.objects.select_related(...).all() loads every deadline row into memory without any limit or pagination. Large deadline datasets cause memory exhaustion and denial of service.

extra.message: Unbounded Database Query in export_documents_csv Without Pagination

metadata.proof: Same pattern as export_matters_csv: Document.objects.select_related(...).all() loads every document row into memory without any limit or pagination. Large document datasets cause memory exhaustion and denial of service.

extra.message: IDOR in client_edit allows modifying any client record

metadata.proof: URL path parameter pk -> get_object_or_404(Client, pk=pk) at line 62; no ownership, assigned-attorney, or tenant check is performed, so any attorney can edit another attorney's client, changing status, contact info, assigned_attorney, etc.

extra.message: Missing authorization scoping exposes all clients in client_list

metadata.proof: GET /clients/ -> query returns every Client object with no tenant or assigned-attorney filter; any attorney/paralegal/firm admin sees the full client directory and conflict notes.

extra.message: IDOR in matter_create allows creating matters for arbitrary clients

metadata.proof: GET /matters/create/?client=<victim_client_id> pre-populates the MatterForm client field (lines 63-66). POST to the same endpoint submits the form, and form.save() at line 58 creates a Matter linked to any client ID with zero authorization checks. An attorney can create matters for clients they do not represent.

extra.message: Unverified profile email change enables cross-client account takeover

metadata.proof: ProfileUpdateForm includes 'email' as a user-modifiable field (accounts/forms.py:16). POST /profile/ with email set to another client's address -> form.save() at line 53 saves it without verification. Views like client_dashboard, client_matters, and client_documents use request.user.email to look up the Client model, granting the attacker access to the victim client's matters and documents.

extra.message: IDOR via user-controlled email in client_matters

metadata.proof: request.user.email (attacker-controlled via the profile update at accounts/views.py:53) -> Client.objects.get(email=...) at line 95 -> client.matters.all() at line 97. A client user who changes their email to a victim's email address gains access to the victim's matters.

extra.message: IDOR via user-controlled email in client_dashboard

metadata.proof: request.user.email (attacker-controlled via profile update) -> Client.objects.get(email=...) at line 239 -> client.matters.all() at line 243 and shared documents at line 244. A client user who changes their email to a victim's email gains access to the victim's dashboard, matters, and shared documents.

extra.message: Account enumeration via disabled-account login message

metadata.proof: An attacker who submits valid credentials for a disabled account reaches form_valid at line 18. line 20 checks is_active_account, and line 21 emits the distinct message 'Your account has been disabled.' The default AuthenticationForm only shows 'Please enter a correct username and password' on invalid credentials, so the discrepancy reveals the account exists but is disabled. Requires valid credentials first, limiting severity.

extra.message: Denial of service via full-file read in document_download

metadata.proof: GET /documents/download/<pk>/ opens the file at version.file.path and calls f.read() at line 129 which loads the entire file into memory before creating the HttpResponse. An attacker who uploads (or has access to) a very large file can exhaust server memory, causing a denial of service.
